children: The Tennessee-based company reported results for the quarter ended July 31.
Revenue Growth Outpaces Expectations
Smith & Wesson posted revenue of $112.6 million, beating the
. Sales rose 32.3% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 28.7% from 25.9%, helped by a $2.9 million tariff refund.

The company swung to GAAP net income of $2.6 million from a $3.4 million loss a year earlier. Operating income also turned positive, reaching $4.2 million compared with an approximately $3.0 million operating loss in the prior-year quarter.
Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDAS nearly doubled to $13.8 million, or 12.2% of sales.
CEO
Mark Smith
said the company is “off to an excellent start to fiscal 2027,” pointing to demand across consumer and professional channels.
CFO
Deana McPherson
said she expects sales for the second quarter roughly 10% above last year, with full-year revenue growth of 5-7% over fiscal 2026.
Dividend Declaration
The board authorized a $0.13-per-share quarterly dividend, payable Oct. 1 to shareholders of record Sep. 17.
The first-quarter beat follows a
in June, when Smith & Wesson topped estimates on both revenue and earnings.

Smith & Wesson Brands has a market capitalization of $550.18 million, a 52-week high of $17.56 and a 52-week low of $8.01.
